title: OneNote for Android: Copilot chat pane with page summaries and questions
summary: Hold: the briefing treats Copilot activity-history storage and prerequisites as undocumented even though Microsoft's general Copilot documentation covers them. The rollout, licence requirement and Cloud Policy control are supported; the licensing checklist also names a control missing from the table.

claims.quote: Microsoft is introducing a new Copilot chat pane in OneNote Mobile (Android) for users licensed with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium).

claims.claim: The Summary feature generates concise summaries of longer OneNote pages.
claims.quote: This update adds a new Summary feature that allows users to generate concise summaries of longer OneNote pages

claims.claim: Users can ask questions about their notes directly within the OneNote mobile app.
claims.quote: as well as ask questions about their notes, directly within the OneNote mobile app.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The notice suggests informing helpdesk staff and users about Copilot chat and Summary in OneNote mobile.
claims.quote: Consider informing helpdesk staff and users about the availability of Copilot chat and the Summary feature in OneNote mobile.

claims.claim: The notice asks administrators to ensure intended users are assigned the Premium licence.
claims.quote: Ensure that users who should access this feature are assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated page for this Android Summary and Q&A pane at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: OneNote Android Copilot chat pane Summary prerequisites license page fair use limits; "OneNote" "Android" "Summary" "Copilot chat pane". Read returned release-note excerpts and the Copilot overview; results describe other features and platforms, not this pane.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot only surfaces organisational data for which the individual user has at least view permissions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot only surfaces organizational data to which individual users have at least view permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's privacy page says prompts and responses from Copilot interactions in apps including OneNote are stored as Copilot activity history.
claims.quote: We refer to the user's prompt and Copilot's response to that prompt as the "content of interactions" and the record of those interactions is the user's Copilot activity history.

claims.claim: The supplied notice itself does not state whether the Android pane stores Copilot activity history.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneNote" "Android" "Copilot" "activity history". Read MC1309746 in full and the Copilot privacy page's interaction-storage section. The notice discusses processing and existing controls, but not activity-history storage; the privacy page does.

claims.where: Open questions: Android activity history; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Whether prompts and responses in this Android Copilot pane are stored as Copilot activity history remains an open question.
claims.quote: When a user interacts with Microsoft Copilot (using apps such as Word, PowerPoint, Excel, OneNote, Loop, or Whiteboard), we store data about these interactions. The stored data includes the user's prompt and Copilot's response
claims.fix: Remove the activity-history bullet from Open questions and remove 'Whether the Android pane does the same is not stated in the notice.' from Risk assessment. Keep the existing statement that Microsoft's Copilot privacy page documents prompt and response storage for Copilot in OneNote; that rule is not limited to another platform.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyse content removes Copilot features in OneNote on Android.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:

claims.claim: The Android policy is named Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content.
claims.quote: Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content

claims.claim: Cloud Policy is required to apply this privacy setting to Office on Android.
claims.quote: To apply any of these four policy settings for Office on Android devices, you need to use Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center route is Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings, where the named policy is selected.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On the Policy configurations page, select Create. ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.

claims.claim: The policy applies to users within the policy configuration's scope, chosen on Choose the scope.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Office Apps Administrator for Cloud Policy administration.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended)

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn API or automation operation is documented for setting this Cloud Policy privacy control as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 Apps API PowerShell Microsoft Graph officeClientConfiguration policy settings; "Cloud Policy" "API" "office" configuration; "Cloud Policy" "Graph" "beta" "configuration". Read Cloud Policy overview and audit-schema excerpts; no setting-write API found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says generative AI responses are not guaranteed to be factual.
claims.quote: The responses that generative AI produces aren't guaranteed to be 100% factual.

claims.claim: Neither the supplied roadmap description nor the notice describes this pane changing notes or taking actions.
claims.quote: Searched: supplied roadmap description and full MC1309746 for note editing, modification and actions; also searched Learn for "OneNote" "Android" "Summary" "Copilot chat pane". The supplied descriptions name summaries and questions, not editing or actions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), which the notice requires, is the full add-on licensed experience.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is the full add-on licensed experience

claims.claim: The Copilot overview says some features of the Premium experience are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is the full add-on licensed experience (some features are subject to fair use limits)

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The supplied notice names no separate meter, charge or feature-specific price for the pane.
claims.quote: Searched: MC1309746 in full for price, charge, billing and meter; searched Learn for OneNote Android Copilot Summary feature price meter fair use limit licensing. Read the Copilot overview and returned excerpts. The notice names the Premium licence but no separate price or meter.

claims.claim: The overview's Usage-based billing capabilities section lists Cowork, Code and Autopilot rather than OneNote.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Cowork ... Microsoft Copilot Code (Frontier) ... Autopilot (Frontier)

claims.claim: A price or fair-use limit specific to this Android pane is not published in the researched Microsoft documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: OneNote Android Copilot Summary feature price meter fair use limit licensing. Read Copilot overview, its returned licensing excerpts, MC1309746 and Limits for features in Microsoft Copilot Chat. None states a price or fair-use limit specific to this pane.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published prerequisites beyond the Premium licence for this feature.
claims.quote: Users need a Microsoft Copilot license and a qualifying prerequisite license. ... Users must have a work or school account in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.fix: Remove 'Microsoft has not published further prerequisites for this feature.' from Scope. Microsoft's general Copilot requirements publish prerequisite licensing and identity requirements; the absence of an Android-pane-specific page does not make those requirements unpublished.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The researched Microsoft documentation does not identify a separate configuration switch dedicated to this Android pane.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneNote" "Android" disable Copilot separate policy chat pane. Read returned release-note and mobile-app configuration excerpts, the Copilot privacy page, Android privacy controls and MC1309746. Found the broad analyse-content control, not a pane-specific setting.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The analyse-content privacy control is broader than this feature and also affects Copilot in other Office apps and on other platforms.
claims.quote: Excel ... OneNote ... Outlook ... PowerPoint ... Word ... This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The governance checklist asks readers to take stock of licence-based access, but the controls table has no corresponding row.
claims.quote: Identify which users hold a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licence and use OneNote on Android, as only they will see the pane. ... The table contains only the connected-experiences control.
claims.fix: Remove the first Before rollout checklist bullet, 'Identify which users hold a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licence and use OneNote on Android, as only they will see the pane.' It names a licensing control absent from the table; retain the verified licence requirement in Cost and licensing and Scope.
